correctness.rationale: Verified the complete pure-equality finite/infinite classification for A^2, including definitions and exact cardinality cases n=1,2,3,4,n>=5: 1,7,16,15,13. Equivariance partitions A^2 into diagonal D and off-diagonal O. Invariant O-kernels have counts 2,6,6,5 respectively: the n=3 orbit is regular S_3 with six subgroups; at n=4 unordered complementary edges add one kernel; for n>=5 connectedness of KG(n,2) excludes this exception. Unmixed kernels give twice the O count. Mixed kernels consist of universal or equivariant O->A maps; the stabilizer-fixed choices are 2,3,2,2 respectively. Independently constructed equality-pattern orbit/bit-row transitivity enumerator yielded 1,7,16,15,13,13 for n=1..6; transitivity uses at most six atom names and the structural argument covers all infinite A. No claim outside parameter-free pure equality or ordered pairs.
